what_its_for: This is a combination birth control pill used to prevent pregnancy. It contains two female hormones — a progestin (desogestrel) and an estrogen (ethinyl estradiol) — that work together to stop ovulation (the release of an egg), thicken cervical mucus to block sperm, and thin the uterine lining. When taken correctly, it is highly effective at preventing pregnancy. Some formulations may also be prescribed by your doctor for other hormone-related conditions.
how_to_take: Take one pill by mouth every day at the SAME TIME each day. This is very important — taking it at the same time helps it work best and reduces side effects like nausea. You can take it with or without food. If nausea bothers you, try taking it at bedtime or with a meal. Your pill pack contains either 21 active (hormone) pills and 7 reminder (inactive/placebo) pills, or a similar arrangement. Follow the arrows on your pack and take pills in order — do not skip pills or take them out of order. Start a new pack the day after you finish the old one, with no days off.
dosing: Take ONE tablet every day for 28 days (one full pill pack). Active hormone pills are taken for the first 21 days, followed by 7 reminder (inactive) pills. Your period will usually come during the reminder pill week. Start your very first pack on the first day of your period (Day 1 start) OR on the first Sunday after your period begins (Sunday start), depending on your doctor's instructions. If you use a Sunday start, use a backup method of birth control (like condoms) for the first 7 days. After finishing one pack, start the next pack immediately the very next day — even if your period is still going.
missed_dose: Missing pills increases your risk of getting pregnant. Here is what to do: If you miss 1 active pill — take it as soon as you remember, even if that means taking 2 pills in one day. Then continue as normal. No backup contraception is needed. If you miss 2 active pills in a row (Week 1 or Week 2) — take 2 pills on the day you remember and 2 pills the next day, then continue one pill per day. Use a backup method (condoms) for 7 days. If you miss 2 active pills in a row in Week 3, OR if you miss 3 or more active pills at any time — throw away the rest of the pack and start a new pack that same day (Day 1 start) or the next Sunday (Sunday start). Use backup contraception for 7 days. If you miss any of the 7 reminder (inactive) pills, throw away the missed pills and keep taking one pill per day. No backup contraception is needed. If you are unsure what to do, use a backup method and call your pharmacist or doctor.
storage: Store at room temperature between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do NOT store in the bathroom. Keep this medication out of reach of children and pets. Do not use if the expiration date on the pack has passed.
what_to_avoid: Do NOT smoke cigarettes while taking this medication, especially if you are over 35 years old. Smoking combined with birth control pills significantly raises your risk of serious blood clots, stroke, and heart attack. Avoid prolonged bed rest or long periods of inactivity (like long flights) without moving around, as this can increase blood clot risk. Some medications can make your birth control pill less effective, including certain seizure medicines (like rifampin, phenytoin, carbamazepine), the herbal supplement St. John's Wort, and some HIV medications. Always tell ALL of your healthcare providers and your pharmacist that you are taking this pill so they can check for interactions. Avoid taking more than one pill per day unless specifically instructed by your doctor.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or go to the emergency room RIGHT AWAY if you experience any of these warning signs (remember the acronym ACHES): Abdominal pain (severe), Chest pain or shortness of breath, Headache (sudden, severe), Eye problems (blurred vision, vision loss), Severe leg pain or swelling. Also call your doctor if you experience: yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice), a lump in your breast, depression or mood changes, no period after finishing a pack (you may be pregnant), severe allergic reaction (rash, swelling of face/throat, difficulty breathing), or blood pressure that is consistently high. Tell your doctor before starting this pill if you have a history of blood clots, stroke, heart disease, migraines with aura, liver problems, or breast cancer.
when_it_works: If you start this pill on the first day of your period (Day 1 start), you are protected from pregnancy right away. If you start on any other day (such as a Sunday start), you must use a backup method of birth control (like condoms) for the first 7 days. It may take 1 to 3 months for your periods to regulate and for some side effects (like spotting or breast tenderness) to settle down. Remember: this medication does NOT protect you against sexually transmitted infections (STIs). Use condoms to protect against STIs.
special_populations: PREGNANCY: Do NOT take this medication if you are pregnant or think you may be pregnant. Stop taking it and call your doctor right away if you become pregnant. BREASTFEEDING: This medication is generally not recommended while breastfeeding, especially in the first 6 weeks after delivery, as the estrogen component may reduce milk supply. Talk to your doctor about alternative options. TEENAGERS: This medication can be used in adolescents after their first menstrual period. Same instructions and risks apply. WOMEN OVER 35 WHO SMOKE: You should NOT use this medication due to a significantly increased risk of heart attack, stroke, and blood clots. OLDER ADULTS: This medication is not intended for use after menopause. LIVER DISEASE: Do not use if you have active liver disease or liver tumors. Always tell your doctor about all medical conditions and all medications, vitamins, and supplements you take.
